teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: The Cartel just set the season's high-water mark, and somehow the bench still stole a headline. Dak Prescott scored 34.3 as a reserve, the biggest bench score anyone has left out all year and the third time Mike D. has stranded a quarterback game of 29 or more; the man owns two quarterbacks and a coin that hates him. This time it cost nothing, because George Pickens, kept for $22, a dollar shy of Mike D.'s favorite number, nearly quadrupled his projection and Ja'Marr Chase feasted on Joe Burrow's four-touchdown night against Pittsburgh. Benching the Steelers defense was the sharpest call of the week, since it finished at minus seven on the wrong end of that same game. Mark is next, and the committee would love to see which quarterback gets the nod, mostly out of curiosity.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: The kids table has a 7-3 record, and the league's last Swish virgin is second in the rankings. Sam is seventh in points, a trick nobody else has figured out, and this week was the full Dootron experience: the eighth-best score in the league, a 9.4-point escape from Frum, and 21 of those points from a Vikings defense the projections ranked 11th of 12. The Queens went into Green Bay and won by 20, with Kirk Lemieux throwing his first touchdown pass since coming home to Minnesota, and Sam, who has spent years insisting that man plays fundamental football, finally got paid for it. Behind Parker Washington the receiver room is Tutu Atwell, picked up Sunday, and a stack of injury tags. He is four weeks from the playoffs, starting with Hess, and nobody at the grown-ups' table is laughing as loudly as they were in September.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: Last week this column called Hess "about as close to a bye as a 6-3 team can draw." Baker played it like one and won by 74.5, the second-biggest margin of the season. The Crustacean once explained that he isn't necessarily here to win, he's here to ruin your weekend; Hess can confirm it's possible to do both. It was a perfect lineup, with not one point left on the bench, from a manager who has made four roster moves all year and treats the waiver wire like a rumor. Jahmyr Gibbs went for 40 in Munich, Chuba Hubbard added 31, and nobody has allowed fewer points than the Dino Nuggets. The reigning champ is next, and he arrives limping.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Hearn told the group chat last week that his squad was way too good to be third in the Black division. Three straight wins later the committee has him fourth with the easiest remaining schedule in the league, so for once the complaining worked. Brock Purdy won the weekend's wildest shootout and scored 31, Deebo Samuel added 24, and the reigning champ never made it a game. The lineup card was still vintage Hearn: he picked up Wan'Dale Robinson on Sunday, started him through a questionable tag for 2.5 while Antonio Williams scored 11 on the bench, and rode a Jaguars defense that posted the worst number of the week in a game Jacksonville won comfortably. Frum is next, then Baker, Hess and Mark, and a team with the second-best all-play record in the league is out of excuses.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Christian McCaffrey's first game as a McButt Nugget produced 44.3 points, the best game any player has had in this league all season. Jordan got him from Hess, along with TreVeyon Henderson, for Rhamondre Stevenson and two players who can't currently suit up, which is less a trade than a mugging with paperwork. Hudson once congratulated Jordan on finally getting one of his 131 trade proposals accepted, and Jordan corrected him: 132. Years of spamming every inbox in the league finally hit, and Trader Perks has been at full chub ever since. Papa also scooped up C.J. Stroud, the quarterback Brett A. cut a week ago, started him for 20, and climbs to fifth with Jeff up next.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: Morgan Wallen has the No. 3 album in the country, and it's called I'm The Problem, which saves the committee some writing. Mark cut Lamar Jackson this week, the pick flagged as his best on draft day, and that left a doubtful Drake Maye as the only quarterback on the roster. Maye started, scored 2.9 and lost by 25 in Munich; the Coladas scored 77, lost to Jeff by 45 and fell two spots. Frum once described a P-Unit draft that began with the two best receivers and ended with six backup running backs, and Mark has since improved on it: eight running backs, zero healthy quarterbacks. Josh Jacobs and Kyle Monangai are out and Bucky Irving was idle, which is how Kaelon Black and Corey Kiner became a starting backfield. The house mouse has gone quiet at the worst possible time, with the first-place Cartel up next.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: Hudson knows this script. He opened his title defense 0-3 and summarized it himself as "Champ - 0-3." This year's Amigos are 5-2 since an 0-3 start, and Sunday was the loudest win yet, a 45-point beating of the team that was ranked fourth. Patrick Mahomes scored 35, Tony Pollard added nearly 20, and the weekly kicker shuffle finally paid off, so much lauve to new arrival Jason Sanders and his 14. Jeff has now made nine pickups this season without spending a dollar of his waiver budget, which is either discipline or a man who lost the password. The schedule turns mean from here, the second-hardest in the league, and it starts with Papa and his new running back.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: Foy set a perfect lineup this week, with every point his roster had to give in the starting nine, and he lost by 60. That's the fadunking of the week, and it's what happens when the bench is a waiting room: Ladd McConkey is out, two more receivers are on IR and three other reserves were idle. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jared Goff did their part from Munich, but Kyren Williams managed 4 on a projection of 17 and Jason Myers kicked 2, because it wouldn't be a Foy season without a kicker problem. It has been three weeks since the last victory Reuben, and the Book of Matthew offers no guidance on what to eat after losing five of six. The Shepherds somehow moved up a spot, only because the reigning champ fell past them, and Danny is next in a game neither team can afford to lose.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: Frum's stat checkers once ruled that Skeets is the Detroit Lions of Fantasy Football. On Sunday the actual Lions won by 25 in Munich, and the fantasy ones scored 72.6, the lowest total of the week and the lowest this season by any team not managed by Hess or Frum. With Saquon Barkley idle, Josh Allen was the only starter who looked like he'd been told there was a game: Chris Olave, Travis Kelce and Tank Dell, a fresh pickup, combined for about 12. The commish also started the Packers defense against the Queens and got 4 while Sam's Vikings scored 21 in the same game, so the man he already owes a herd's worth of steak dinners beat him without even being on the schedule. Phoebe Bridgers was the musical guest on SNL this weekend, so at least the soundtrack fit. The champ is 5-5 and ninth with the hardest remaining schedule in the league, and Baker, who is here to ruin weekends, is first up.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Danny has grounds to declare FRAUD and refuse to concede, and this time the committee would hear the case. Los Desperados have the fourth-most points in the league and the third-best all-play record, and they are 3-7. He once warned that playing the Grimies was essentially a bye week; these days playing Danny is how you set a personal best, and Jordan just posted his highest score of the season against him. Danny scored 120, the fifth-best total in the league, with Joe Burrow throwing four touchdowns, and lost by 37. Utah's Devon Dampier has been building a Heisman case mostly out of sight, and Danny knows what it's like to do good work nobody rewards. He is two games behind the 5-5 teams with four to play, and Foy is next.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Even the Chargers won this week, ending an 0-8 start on Monday night, which leaves Frum and Hess as the last ones in the building still stuck on two wins. D Lee once celebrated a victory by announcing that the Butts "still looked like ass but ultimately passed the smell test." This year's team has passed it twice. The Bellies lost the closest game of the week, 9.4 to Sam, and here's the cruel part: the best lineup Frum could possibly have set would have scored 107, and Sam scored 107.2. Emmett Johnson, a September waiver pickup, scored 32 and deserved better company, while Bryce Young managed 8 and Kenneth Walker, the $39 keeper, sat out. At 2-8 the job now is spoiling other people's seasons, and Hearn's three-game win streak is the first target.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Hess is open for business, and the business is next year. He sent Christian McCaffrey and TreVeyon Henderson to Papa for Rhamondre Stevenson, Jeremiyah Love and Carnell Tate, and the early returns are brutal: McCaffrey scored 44 for the Nuggets, Stevenson scored 1 for Hess, and Love and Tate can't play. Ebenezer is the No. 1 movie in the country, and Jerome has skipped straight to the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come. He once typed "i have no players left" in the middle of a Sunday; this time he got there on purpose. He remains the only manager in league history with a rule named after him, and it is not a compliment. The present is grim: a 74.5-point loss to Baker, his fifth straight, five players on IR or ruled out, and a Toilet Bowl seat with his name already on it. Sam is next, so bring a helmet.

commentary.intro: Texas beat No. 8 LSU by a point on Saturday on a late Arch Manning touchdown pass. Fadunkadunk did not get the memo: five of this week's six games were decided by 37 points or more, and three of the four highest scores of the season landed on the same weekend. Mike D. hung 169.9 on Foy, the best total anyone has posted all year, and Jordan and Baker both cleared 155. The NFL set the tone when San Francisco and Dallas combined for 86 points, and the loudest number of all belonged to Christian McCaffrey, who scored 44.3 in his first start as a McButt Nugget, days after Hess traded him away. The top three hold their spots, Hearn and Jordan each climb one, and Mark and the reigning champ each fall two, Mark after starting a quarterback with a doubtful tag and Brett A. after posting the lowest score of the week. And Sam is 7-3 with a losing all-play record, carried this week by the Vikings defense, which is the most Sam sentence the committee has ever written.

awards.highScore: Mike D. scored 169.9, the best total of the season by nearly 11 points, and did it with Dak Prescott's 34.3 on the bench, which happens to be the best bench score of the season. The Cartel now holds both records at once.
awards.bust: Mark cut Lamar Jackson this week, which left Drake Maye as the only quarterback on the roster, doubtful tag and all. Maye played, scored 2.9 on a projection near 22, and New England lost by 25 in Munich.
awards.bestDefense: The Vikings were the 11th-ranked defense of 12 by projection. Sam started them anyway, because of course he did, and they scored 21 in a 20-point win at Green Bay, tied for the best defensive score anyone has started this season. Sam won by 9.4. Do the math.
awards.benchBomb: Dak Prescott scored 34.3 on Mike D.'s bench while Jayden Daniels started and scored 20.6. It's the third time this season the Cartel has left a quarterback game of 29 or more in the garage, and this one didn't cost a thing.
awards.boom: George Pickens, the $22 keeper, scored 38 on a projection under 10, the biggest boom of the week.
awards.lowScore: Brett A., 72.6, the lowest score this season by any team not managed by Hess or Frum.
awards.luckiestWin: Sam won with the eighth-best score of the week because Frum brought the ninth.
awards.toughestLoss: Danny scored 120.7, fifth-best of the week and the third-highest losing score of the season, and lost by 37 because he drew Jordan on the day McCaffrey arrived.
awards.blowout: Baker over Hess by 74.5, the second-biggest margin of the season. Hess was on the wrong end of the biggest one too.
awards.closest: Sam over Frum by 9.4, and the best lineup Frum could have set would have scored 107 against Sam's 107.2. Even perfect loses by a fifth of a point.
awards.questionableStart: Hearn picked up Wan'Dale Robinson on Sunday and started him through a questionable tag for 2.5 while Antonio Williams scored 11 on the bench.
awards.worstDefense: Hearn's Jaguars scored 3, the worst defensive number of the week, in a game Jacksonville won by 17.

commentary.outro:
Week 11 headliner: Mike D. against Mark, first against sixth, the highest-scoring team in the league against one that currently has no healthy quarterback. Jordan and his new running back get Jeff, who has won five of his last seven. Baker draws the reigning champ, Hearn gets Frum, and Foy and Danny meet in a game the loser probably doesn't come back from. Sam plays Hess, which should tell us whether lightning needs a second strike.

Trade Desk: the league's trade deadline is Wednesday, so this is last call. The deal of the season is already on the books: Jordan got the best individual game of the year in the first week of the McCaffrey trade, and Hess got a head start on next August. For everyone else the shopping list is short. Mark needs a quarterback before Wednesday and has five receivers to pay with; Hearn has Caleb Williams sitting on his bench and a receiver room held together by questionable tags behind Deebo Samuel. Williams for Tee Higgins fixes both teams in one phone call. Baker has Aaron Rodgers doing nothing behind Trevor Lawrence if Mark wants a second option. Foy has Blake Corum, Jonah Coleman and Dylan Sampson in the backfield and almost nothing healthy at receiver behind Amon-Ra St. Brown and DK Metcalf, and Danny, his opponent this week, has Rome Odunze and DeMario Douglas on the bench, a deal worth making before they play each other. Move of the week: Jordan trading for McCaffrey and getting 44.3 on the first try. Anti-move of the week: Mark cutting Lamar Jackson and then starting a doubtful Drake Maye for 2.9. Honorable mention to Jeff, whose kicker swap finally produced more than a lateral. Time stamp: Trader Perks sends a dozen more offers before the window closes, and the house mouse answers none of them.

Luck Index: Sam is 7-3 with a losing all-play record, about two wins ahead of what his scoring has earned. Danny is 3-7 with the third-best all-play record, about three wins behind. By the committee's expected-wins count Danny should be ahead of Sam, and instead they are separated by eight spots and four games. Baker is the other beneficiary, nearly two wins to the good, though a perfect 155-point lineup is a fine way to change the subject. Keeper Corner returns in Week 12. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
